what.text: AOD-9604 is a 16-amino-acid peptide made from the tail end of human growth hormone (amino acids 177 to 191), with one extra tyrosine added at the start to make it more stable. It was developed in Australia by Metabolic Pharmaceuticals as a possible obesity drug.

Cox HD, et al. Drug Test Anal 2015

what.text: How it acts, according to animal and lab studies

items.text: In obese mice and rats, it reduced weight gain and body fat and increased fat breakdown, without raising blood sugar the way whole growth hormone does.

src.label: Ng FM, et al. Horm Res 2000
Heffernan MA, et al. Int J Obes 2001

items.text: Unlike growth hormone, it did not bind the growth hormone receptor or make cells multiply in lab tests.

src.label: Heffernan MA, et al. Int J Obes 2001

items.text: In mice it raised levels of a fat-cell receptor (beta-3 adrenergic), but its fat-burning effect did not depend on that receptor alone.

src.label: Heffernan M, et al. Endocrinology 2001

items.text: In human fat tissue in the lab, the related fragment AOD-9401 increased fat breakdown and lowered fat build-up.

src.label: Heffernan MA, et al. Am J Physiol 2000

what.text: None of these mechanisms has been shown to cause weight loss in people.

research.text: Six company-funded placebo-controlled trials in about 900 people ran in Australia from 2001 to 2006. The one published paper on them, written by staff of a firm consulting for the developer, reports safety only. It does not report whether people lost weight. No Phase 3 trial was found, and ClinicalTrials.gov lists no trial of AOD-9604.

The paper says the two largest trials were notified to Australia's TGA under its Clinical Trial Notification scheme. The authors declared ties to the developer: one held shares in its parent company Calzada, one was a consultant and former medical director, and the writer's firm consulted for the company. Metabolic Pharmaceuticals funded all 6 trials.

research.title: 6 safety and dose trials, 893 people (Stier et al., 2013 summary)

facts.v: 6 randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials, summarised in one paper
893 adults; all but the first were obese but otherwise healthy; the first 4 trials enrolled men only

single IV doses (15 healthy men; 23 obese men); single oral doses (17 obese men); 7 days by mouth (36 obese men); 12 weeks by mouth (300 adults); 24 weeks of tablets at 0.25, 0.5 or 1 mg/day (502 adults)
side effects, vital signs, blood tests, ECG, IGF-1, glucose tolerance, antibodies

research.found: The paper reports no rise in IGF-1, no worsening of glucose tolerance and no anti-AOD-9604 antibodies in the people tested. Side effects were reported as similar to placebo, with no serious adverse event judged related to the drug. The two Phase IIb trials were designed to measure weight loss, but the paper gives no weight results.

src.label: Stier H, Vos E, Kenley D. J Endocrinol Metab 2013 (full text)

research.title: Oral fragment in obese mice and human fat tissue (Heffernan et al.)

facts.v: animal study plus lab tests on fat tissue
obese (ob/ob) mice: 8 on saline, 10 on the fragment AOD-9401, by mouth
30 days
weight gain, food intake, fat-tissue activity, energy use

research.found: From day 16, weight gain was lower on the fragment. Food intake did not differ. In isolated fat tissue from obese rodents and humans, fat breakdown rose and fat build-up fell.

src.label: Heffernan MA, et al. Am J Physiol 2000

research.title: Oral AOD-9604 in obese Zucker rats (Ng et al.)

facts.v: animal study
obese Zucker rats
19 days
weight gain; fat-tissue activity; insulin sensitivity

research.found: Weight gain was about half that of controls (15.8 g vs 35.6 g). Unlike growth hormone, it did not harm insulin sensitivity.

src.label: Ng FM, et al. Horm Res 2000

research.title: AOD-9604 vs growth hormone in obese and lean mice (Heffernan et al.)

facts.v: animal study with lab tests on cells with the growth hormone receptor
obese and lean mice, given growth hormone, AOD-9604 or saline by pump
14 days
weight, energy use, fat burning, blood sugar and insulin; receptor binding

research.found: Both growth hormone and AOD-9604 reduced weight gain in obese mice and raised fat burning. AOD-9604 did not cause high blood sugar, did not bind the growth hormone receptor and did not make cells multiply.

src.label: Heffernan MA, et al. Int J Obes 2001

research.title: Knee injections in rabbits with arthritis (Kwon and Park)

facts.v: randomized animal study
32 rabbits with chemically induced knee arthritis
weekly knee injections in weeks 4 to 7; assessed at week 8
cartilage damage; limping

research.found: Cartilage scores and limping were better with AOD-9604, hyaluronic acid or both than with saline, and best with both.

us.text: AOD-9604 is not FDA approved for any use. FDA lists it among compounding nominations that were withdrawn, with safety concerns. It is not in the HHS peptide compounding policy of October 2026. As of November 1, 2026.

items.text: none. No approved drug contains AOD-9604; the furthest trials found were Phase IIb.

src.label: Stier H, Vos E, Kenley D. J Endocrinol Metab 2013 (full text)

items.text: FDA's Category 2 page lists AOD-9604 under bulk drug substances that were nominated for compounding but withdrawn by the nominators, and that were previously in category 2. FDA says it may pose a significant risk of immune reactions for some routes, may have impurity problems, and that FDA has no or only limited safety information. FDA has also identified serious adverse events that may be linked to it, though cause is not clear.

world.lead: No regulator has approved AOD-9604 as a medicine. Australia, where it was developed, lists it as a prescription-only poison that is illegal to possess without authority. WADA bans it at all times.

after.text: AOD-9604 is named on the WADA 2026 Prohibited List in class S2.2.3 (growth hormone, its analogues and fragments) as an example of a growth hormone fragment. It is banned at all times, in and out of competition. It is still named on the 2027 List, which takes effect January 1, 2027. A 2015 anti-doping lab paper describes a urine test for it.

side.text: The only published human safety data come from the developer's own trials, which reported side effects similar to placebo. FDA says it lacks enough safety information and has identified serious adverse events that may be linked to AOD-9604. No fertility study was found.

items.text: in the first IV trial, 12 of 15 men reported 29 mild or moderate side effects, most often headache, tiredness, low blood sugar and dizziness, spread across AOD-9604 and placebo. No serious adverse events occurred.
